items.title: Parang-wielding duo rob taxi driver, friend during drinks outside eatery
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A taxi driver and his female friend were held at knifepoint by two men who robbed them of cash and valuables worth about RM3,000 while they were having drinks outside an eatery here recently. Kong said more than 10 of his friends had been at the eatery earlier, but they gradually left, leaving him and his friend behind. Kong said his friend later recalled seeing one of the suspects entering and leaving an electronic gaming centre next to the eatery several days before the robbery.

items.title: Man drowns during outing with 13 friends at forest reserve waterfall
items.summary: Mohd Aiman Nazmi Mohd Yusuf, 29, from Felda Endau, Johor, was pronounced dead at the scene. Pahang Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Mohd Salahuddin Isa said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 1.29pm. He said Health Ministry personnel who also arrived at the scene later confirmed that the victim had died.

items.title: KLVC land deal: Ex-senior Felda officer to be charged tomorrow [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A former senior Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) officer, who was previously investigated over the alleged misappropriation of the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project, will be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court tomorrow. The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) confirmed that it had obtained approval to charge the former Felda officer. The KLVC investigation is part of seven investigation papers involving Felda and Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC), comprising six new investigation papers and one previous investigation.

items.title: Man held with 2,000 suspected yaba pills in Gua Musang
items.summary: GUA MUSANG: Police arrested a 49-year-old man and seized about 2,000 pills believed to be yaba, weighing 200g and estimated to be worth RM30,000, during a check at Km18 of Jalan Gua Musang-Kuala Lipis yesterday. Gua Musang district police chief Superintendent Sik Choon Foo said the suspect was arrested about 6pm after allegedly attempting to flee when his Toyota Vios was stopped for checks by a mobile patrol vehicle (MPV) unit from the Gua Musang District Police Headquarters. He said police pursued and detained the suspect before searching the vehicle and discovering the suspected yaba pills.

items.title: Slovak school stabbing kills teacher, injures two
items.summary: BRATISLAVA: A knife-wielding schoolboy killed a teacher and wounded another and a pupil in an attack in northwestern Slovakia on Tuesday, authorities said. A 13-year-old schoolboy was detained over the attack, police said, adding that he was being investigated for murder. "This morning, after the first class, a school pupil launched a knife attack," Interior Minister Matus Sutaj Estok told reporters.

items.title: Orphaned siblings killed days after asking photographer to reprint family photos
items.summary: Their uncle, Abd Malik Yahaya, 55, said he never expected Hakimah's visit to his home yesterday to be their last meeting. "They had lived independently since their parents died. Their father died when Hakimah was still in primary school, while their mother died in 2013.

items.title: Kim Loong lowers production target by 6 pct to 310,000 tonnes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kim Loong Resources Bhd had lowered its production target for fresh fruit bunches (FFB) of oil palm by six per cent to 310,000 tonnes for the financial year ending Jan 31, 2027 (FY27). During the quarter, Kim Loong registered five per cent lower net profits of RM44.94 million, compared with RM47.3 million in the corresponding quarter, on the back of three per cent lower revenue of RM422.76 million. Nevertheless, 14 per cent higher average FFB price during the quarter softened the impact.

items.title: Air Astana to launch Almaty-Langkawi flights in December
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Air Astana will launch seasonal direct flights between Almaty and Langkawi from Dec 25, 2026 to March 27, 2027, marking the Kazakh flag carrier's return to Malaysia with its own scheduled services. The return flight, KC8168, will leave Langkawi at 9.40am and arrive in Almaty at 2.40pm, with a flight time of eight hours. Air Astana launched its first direct Almaty-Kuala Lumpur flight in October 2009.

items.title: Newsweek ranks Sunway Medical Centre No. 1 in Malaysia for paediatrics
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Medical Centre in has been ranked No. Sunway Medical Centre said the recognition comes as it expands its paediatric services with the opening of Tower F, a dedicated 216-bed children's tower. The new tower expands the centre's paediatric services, including specialised inpatient care and subspecialties, while complementing its children's health and development Centre, paediatric intensive care unit and 24-hour children's walk-in and emergency department.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines expands codeshare partnership with China Southern
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines and China Southern Airlines will expand their codeshare partnership to cover five additional routes between Malaysia and China from Oct 25. Malaysia Airlines and China Southern first launched their codeshare cooperation on the Kuala Lumpur-Guangzhou route in July 2023, before expanding it to Kuala Lumpur-Beijing Daxing, Kuala Lumpur-Shanghai Pudong and Penang-Guangzhou in July 2024. Malaysia Airlines has also launched new services from Kuala Lumpur to Chengdu, Shenzhen and Changsha this year, while China Southern has increased capacity on its Kuala Lumpur-Guangzhou and Kuala Lumpur-Shenzhen routes.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines -September 29, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Here are today's top stories. Real problem Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has questioned why Transport Minister Anthony Loke was being singled out over his offer to resign, arguing that corruption and plunder are the nation's real issues. Repatriation Malaysia today launched the first phase of a repatriation programme involving 1,476 Myanmar detainees, who are being sent home aboard three Myanmar naval vessels, including a hospital ship.

items.title: VS narrows net loss in Q4 to RM22mil as revenue rises
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: VS Industry Bhd reported a smaller net loss of RM22 million in the fourth quarter ended July 31, 2026 (Q4 FY26), than RM33 million a year earlier, as revenue increased 16.3 per cent year-on-year to RM998.6 million. However, the electronic manufacturing services group recorded a net loss of RM53.82 million for FY26, compared with a net profit of RM36.71 million a year earlier, as VS is affected by lower orders from key customers affected by soft consumer sentiments globally, it said. VS Industry said the weaker order intake affected overall production capacity utilisation, while customers also implemented cost optimisation measures.

items.title: After Finance Ministry says no duty due on K8 cargo, Maritime Network asks Customs dept to put ruling on record
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Maritime Network Sdn Bhd is seeking a written explanation from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM) following a meeting with the Ministry of Finance (MOF) over the handling of Atlanta crude discharged at Tanjung Langsat under a K8 declaration. At the September 25 discussion, chaired by MOF Tax Division Under-Secretary Datuk John Patrick Antonysamy and attended by JKDM officers, the chair said no duty was due on the cargo as presented. Maritime has also separately raised questions about another Atlanta crude cargo carried by MT Marlin Santorini.

items.title: UiTM Holdings losses not unknown to university management, says former VC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Financial problems affecting UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd, which resulted in millions of ringgit in losses, were not unknown to the university's management but had been discussed and monitored at the highest levels, a former university vice-chancellor said. Professor Datuk Dr Roziah Mohd Janor said UiTM Holdings' management was required to regularly present financial reports to the company's board of directors before they were brought to the university management and Board of Directors. "The management was aware of the matter, and the crisis faced by UiTM Holdings had been discussed at the university management level.

items.title: Crescendo's Q2 net profit more than quadruples on data centre land sale
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Crescendo Corporation Bhd recorded a net profit of RM70.6 million for the second quarter ended July 31, 2026 (Q2 FY27), more than four times the level in the same quarter last year, boosted by the land sales to data centre developers in Kota Tinggi, Johor. The net profit came on the back of a 158 per cent surge in revenue to RM210.43 million in Q2 FY27, Crescendo said in Bursa Malaysia filing. The operating environment is expected to remain challenging due to ongoing geopolitical tensions, volatility in global supply chains and energy markets as well as rising construction costs, said Crescendo.

items.title: From CPR to comfort: The doctor who stayed by Dr Mahathir's side
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: As Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad bade his final farewell to his late wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali, yesterday, three medical personnel stayed close by, watching over the former prime minister. [[nid:1544092]] Dr Iskandar, 40, said he was tasked with caring for Dr Mahathir throughout the funeral. The team is headed by Datuk Dr Amin Ariff Nuruddin and Datuk Dr Ahmad Khairuddin Mohamed Yusof; and also included Datuk Dr Ghazali Ahmad; Dr Hafidz Abd Hadi; Dr Hisham Md Sharom; Dr Afif Ashaari; and himself.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Tuesday, September 29, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. items.title: Six escape unhurt after tree falls onto two cars
items.summary: IPOH: Six people escaped unhurt after a tree fell onto two cars along Jalan Simpang Pulai-Lahat near Station 18 here today. Perak Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received a distress call at 4.26pm. He said a team from the Pasir Puteh Fire and Rescue Station arrived at the scene three minutes later.

items.title: Sern Kou winding up plywood business
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sern Kou Resources Bhd will cease the plywood manufacturing operations of its 51 per cent-owned subsidiary Sern Kou Plywood Sdn Bhd, which has been making losses since the financial year 2024. Sern Kou Plywood recorded revenue of RM12.43 million for the unaudited financial year ended June 30, 2026 (FY26), down from RM17.38 million a year earlier. Following the cessation, Sern Kou Plywood will progressively wind down its operations, including realising inventories, collecting receivables, settling liabilities and contractual commitments, and dealing with its property, plant and equipment.

items.title: Sarawak vaccinates 3,579 dogs, distributes 2,281 oral rabies vaccine baits in latest drive
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 29 — A total of 3,579 dogs have been vaccinated through Sarawak’s recent field rabies vaccination efforts this year, alongside the distribution of 2,281 oral rabies vaccine (ORV) baits, said Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg. He said the ORV programme provided an important last-mile approach to reaching free-roaming dogs that were difficult to capture and vaccinate through conventional methods. Abang Johari said Sarawak continued to strengthen its rabies prevention and control measures through vaccination, surveillance, enforcement, public awareness and collaboration with its partners.

items.title: Police trace drug ring that recruited five Malaysians held in Jakarta
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are tracing a drug trafficking syndicate in the country believed to have recruited five Malaysians as drug mules before they were detained by Indonesian authorities in Jakarta last Friday. Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the suspects, four men and a woman aged between 21 and 30, were detained at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport. Hussein said police had received information from the Directorate of Narcotics Crime (Dittipidnarkoba), Criminal Investigation Agency (Bareskrim), Indonesian National Police (POLRI), regarding the detention of the five Malaysians.

items.title: Haze returns to KL as Cheras, Batu Muda hit unhealthy levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Cheras and Batu Muda recorded unhealthy air quality as of 6pm today, with their Air Pollutant Index (API) readings rising from the morning. Cheras recorded an API reading of 171, up from 158 at 8.30am, while Batu Muda rose to 157 from 100. The capital was among 36 areas nationwide recording unhealthy readings, nine more than in the morning.

items.title: Home minister: Government resolving persistent refugee problem according to rule of law
items.summary: He said that a total of 5,000 Myanmar refugees have been finalised to undergo a voluntary and phased repatriation programme back to their country of origin, based on the Myanmar government’s agreement to accept them and the individuals’ consent to return voluntarily. “Today, a total of 1,476 individuals began the First Phase of repatriation, based on the list submitted by the Myanmar Government through an official Diplomatic Note. This resolution was also achieved through diplomatic approaches and direct negotiations with the Myanmar Government,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Sept 29 designated Malaysian Professionals Day
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has agreed to designate Sept 29 as Malaysian Professionals Day. "When it was proposed that Sept 29 be Malaysian Professionals Day, I agreed because it makes sense and serves a purpose," he said. He said the professional class was central to national progress, adding that political leaders, civil servants and professionals had to work as one team.

items.title: Second student arrested over death of Form Two student in Kuala Pilah
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Police have arrested another 16-year-old male student to assist in the investigation into the death of a Form Two student in Kuala Pilah last Friday. Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the latest suspect was a student at the same school and was brought to the Kuala Pilah magistrate's court yesterday for a six-day remand order until Oct 3 to assist investigations. "The victim was also struck on several parts of his body.

items.title: Man assaults motorcyclist after baby's sleep disturbed by loud exhaust
items.summary: Mersing district police chief Superintendent Abdul Razak Abdullah Sani said police received information about the incident after a 1-minute-45-second video of it went viral on social media. "The suspect then assaulted the victim. Abdul Razak said police opened an investigation paper and investigated the case under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB seen leaving palace after nearly three-hour audience with Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 29 —Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim concluded an audience with the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, at Istana Hinggap here after spending nearly three hours at the palace. Earlier, vehicles carrying Undang Luak Sungai Ujong Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari and Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid were also seen entering the palace grounds. The affected Exco members are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.

items.title: Domestic projects will continue to anchor Gamuda's earnings next year
items.summary: Its net profit rose 5.2 per cent in Q4 FY26 to RM349.7 million, driven mainly by stronger contributions from its domestic construction projects, while revenue jumped 19 per cent year-on-year to RM5.76 billion. For the full financial year, net profit rose five per cent to RM1.05 billion from RM1 billion, while revenue increased 14 per cent to a record RM18.6 billion from RM15.97 billion. Domestic construction earnings surged 49 per cent to RM461 million, while total construction earnings, including overseas projects, rose 19 per cent to RM742 million.

items.title: Ringgit ends marginally higher against US dollar, S&P Rating supports sentiment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit strengthened marginally against the US dollar on Tuesday, with market sentiment supported by S&P Global Ratings' reaffirmation of Malaysia's 'A-' sovereign credit rating with a stable outlook. Meanwhile, Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US dollar remained supported, with the US Dollar Index (DXY) rising 0.19 per cent to 101.391 points. He said higher US Treasury yields suggested that US Treasury bonds had become more attractive, while expectations of further interest rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve could also make the US dollar more appealing to investors as interest rate differentials continued to favour US dollar-denominated assets.

items.title: PM Anwar: Malaysian government to continue talks with Myanmar on refugee status
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the Malaysian government will continue engaging with Myanmar to find an amicable solution to the long-standing issue of refugees. He said the issue, which has remained unresolved for decades, had become more complicated as the number of refugees increased, including through negotiations on their possible return. He said without resolve and negotiations, it may lead to protests.

items.title: Aeon Credit Q2 net profit falls to RM59.3mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Aeon Credit Service (M) Bhd's net profit fell to RM59.3 million in the second quarter (Q2) ended Aug 31, 2026, against RM72.23 million a year ago. Revenue rose to RM665.19 million from RM617.88 million previously, supported by the stronger loan and financing growth. For the first half of the financial year ended Feb 28, 2027 (1H FY27), Aeon Credit posted a higher net profit of RM154.46 million versus RM149.77 million previously.

items.title: PM Anwar: Professional expertise must go beyond specialisation to bring Malaysia forward
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today called on Malaysia’s professional community to move beyond narrow specialisation and work across disciplines. He said expertise alone was insufficient to drive the country’s progress. “What is great about professional life is that it brings together people from different disciplines, different races and different regions,” he said when launching the Professional Conference and Exhibition 2026 (PROFEX 2026) in conjunction with the Malaysia Professional Day.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM SEPT 29, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia closed lower as global risk-off sentiment intensified, with Brent crude remaining around US$105 a barrel amid surging US Treasury yields. On the currency front, the ringgit ended slightly stronger against the US dollar at 4.0770. Bitcoin hovered at around RM341,741, while Ethereum stood at around RM11,034.

items.title: PM Anwar says will ‘discuss’ transport minister’s plan to resign
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has said today he will discuss Anthony Loke’s decision step down as Transport Minister. This comes after the Prime Minister receiving Loke’s letter of resignation yesterday. Earlier today, Loke said he will stay on as transport minister until former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak begins his house arrest.

items.title: Scientex to acquire 70pct interest in China's Mintpack for RM102mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Scientex Bhd, through its wholly-owned subsidiary Scientex Packaging (Ayer Keroh) Bhd (SPAK), has entered into a sale and purchase agreement to acquire a 70 per cent stake in China-based Hunan Changcheng Mint New Material Technology Co., Ltd. (Mintpack). The proposed acquisition involves a purchase consideration of RMB167.3 million, about RM101.5 million, said Scientex in a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Tuesday. Scientex views the acquisition as a strategic avenue to expand the group's consumer packaging footprint into China.

items.title: Why do so many Malaysians ride motorcycles?
items.summary: FOR many riders, the motorcycle is solving a practical problem. In 2024, 78.1 per cent of Malaysian households owned a motorcycle. For that rider, the motorcycle is not simply transport.

items.title: Missing Orang Asli woman found dead in Rompin swamp
items.summary: ROMPIN: The search for a missing 73-year-old Orang Asli woman ended today when her body was found in a swampy area in Kampung Lesung, Kedaik, police said. The remains of Kuang Poh, who was last seen leaving her home for a fishing trip on Sept 22, were found at 11.50am. Rompin district police chief Superintendent Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said search and rescue (SAR) team members found Kuang's decomposed remains about 500 metres from where she was last seen.

items.title: UN concerned by Malaysia returns of Myanmar migrants
items.summary: GENEVA, Sept 29 — The UN voiced worry today as Malaysia started sending thousands of Myanmar nationals back to the war-torn country, warning that conditions there would not enable “safe, dignified and sustainable returns”. Malaysia began repatriating around 1,500 Myanmar nationals today, launching the first phase of a return programme that has raised concerns from rights groups. The group is the first of 5,000 Myanmar nationals that Malaysia says have agreed to “voluntary” repatriation from detention centres.

items.title: Women’s ministry: Victims of sexual harassment need to speak up, no shame in it
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Sept 29 —The Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) is calling on students to know their boundaries, dare to say no, and seek help if they face sexual harassment or violence. We also want to teach them how to seek help when someone faces sexual harassment or violence. Lim said bullying, sexual harassment and violence require a cross-ministry approach, covering advocacy, prevention, awareness and counselling.

items.title: Heavy rain, gusty winds expected across peninsula and Sarawak until 7pm, warns MetMalaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for several states in Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak, with thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds expected until 7pm today. In Peninsular Malaysia, the warning covers Penang, Perak and Melaka, as well as parts of five other states. In Sarawak, the warning covers Sri Aman, Betong, Sarikei (Sarikei and Maradong), Sibu (Sibu), Samarahan (Sebuyau) and Kapit (Song).

items.title: Woman found unconscious behind a building in Sabah dies
items.summary: PENAMPANG, Sept 29 — A 38-year-old local woman died after she was found unconscious on the ground behind a building in Donggongon here yesterday. Penampang police chief Supt Sammy Newton said police received a report on the incident at about 12.36pm. Those with information are urged to contact the investigating officer, Penampang police station chief Insp Ahmad Amir Fitri Ab Rahman at 016-449 2215.

items.title: DVS tests 18 dogs following rabies scare in Kedah’s Changlun
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — The Kedah Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) has collected samples from 18 dogs in Changlun, Kedah, and surrounding areas for rabies confirmatory testing as of yesterday, following an incident where a man was bitten by a stray dog in the area. Subsequently, Kedah DVS conducted an on-site investigation and carried out operations to capture stray dogs in collaboration with the Kubang Pasu Municipal Council to locate the suspected animal and assess the potential presence of the rabies virus. Kedah DVS is continuing its investigation and awaiting laboratory results to confirm the presence of rabies among dogs in Kedah,” the statement read.

items.title: Home Ministry: 1,476 Myanmar nationals leave Malaysia in first ‘voluntary’ repatriation phase
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — A total of 1,476 Myanmar nationals departed Malaysia today under the first phase of a “voluntary” repatriation programme aimed at resolving a protracted, decades-long refugee and undocumented migrant challenge, the Home Ministry (KDN) announced. The operation is being conducted by sea via two naval vessels and a hospital ship deployed by the Myanmar government, coordinated jointly by KDN, the Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM), and relevant security agencies. KDN stated that as of Aug 15, a total of 10,388 Myanmar nationals held across Immigration detention depots nationwide have been undergoing biometric identification, immigration status assessments, and security screenings.

items.title: MACC: Ex-senior exec to be charged over RM42m UiTM Holdings loss
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — A former senior executive of a corporation will be charged in court this Thursday in connection with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigation into losses incurred by UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd, including allegations of abuse of power regarding operational expense payments to several companies totalling about RM42 million. “The arrest follows an investigation conducted by MACC regarding issues concerning losses suffered by UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd (UiTM Holdings) in 2023,” the statement read. Meanwhile, MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrest when contacted and stated that the case is being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: Guan Eng says foreign workers should be excluded from minimum wage hike, calls for EPF levy repeal
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 29 — DAP chairman Lim Guan Eng today called on the government to exclude foreign workers from any increase in Malaysia’s minimum wage, arguing that the move would help protect local businesses, particularly micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), from rising operating costs. While acknowledging the rationale for higher wages, Lim said the prospect of a minimum wage increase has sparked concern among local businesses already grappling with intense competition, higher compliance costs and taxes, as well as price pressures from overseas producers. According to Lim, exempting foreign workers from minimum wage increases and scrapping the EPF contribution requirement would help ease cost pressures on local businesses and safeguard the viability of approximately 1.2 million MSMEs nationwide.

items.title: Public to get live access to Sabah 40pc revenue appeal at Kota Kinabalu court
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 29 — Up to 250 members of the public will be able to follow the Court of Appeal hearing on Sabah’s constitutional 40 per cent revenue entitlement next month through a live audiovisual transmission at the Kota Kinabalu Court Complex. The arrangement will allow members of the public to watch the proceedings from the court’s conference hall while the appeal is heard inside the courtroom on Oct 29. The Court of Appeal is scheduled to hear the federal government’s appeal against the High Court’s October 17, 2025 decision in the judicial review brought by the Sabah Law Society (SLS).

items.title: Marina Mahathir: My father healthy but lonely after loss of beloved wife
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad is coping with a deep sense of loneliness following the death of his wife, Tun Dr Hasmah Mohd Ali, whom he shared more than seven decades of marriage with, according to their daughter, Datuk Marina Mahathir. Berita Harian reported that Marina said her 101-year-old father remains in good health but is grieving the loss of his lifelong companion, who died yesterday at the age of 100. He feels lonely,” Marina told reporters after visiting Dr Hasmah’s grave at Pusara Negara in Presint 20 today.

items.title: Dr M recalls shock at wife Dr Hasmah’s sudden passing despite signs of good health
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Sept 29 — Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad has said he did not expect his wife, Tun Dr Hasmah Ali, to pass away yesterday, recalling that she had appeared to be in good health the night before. Dr Mahathir also thanked the royal family for making the journey from Pahang to offer their condolences. Dr Hasmah died at about 9.25am yesterday at the National Heart Institute.

items.title: Nanta: New Johor Bahru court complex among 11 judicial projects worth RM736m nationwide
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 29 — The new Johor Bahru court complex in Kota Iskandar is among 11 judicial infrastructure projects being developed nationwide with a cumulative value of RM736 million, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said today. “The Johor Bahru court complex project was approved by the Economic Planning Unit (EPU) of the Prime Minister's Department back in 2018 under the 11th Malaysia Plan. Also present at the event was Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.

items.title: Fahmi: Only register for medicine delivery service through MoH to avoid scams on Facebook, TikTok
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — Applications for the government's medicine delivery service (UMP) should be done only through the Ministry of Health, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today as he cautioned against possible scam attempts. "I remind everyone there is no registration process other than at health clinics or Ministry of Health facilities only." Patients in Malaysia will soon be able to receive their follow-up medication delivered directly to their doorstep free of charge, following a joint funding initiative announced today by the Communications Ministry and the Health Ministry.

items.title: PM Anwar congratulates Kelantan Sultan on 57th birthday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim extended his heartfelt congratulations to the Sultan of Kelantan, Sultan Muhammad V, on the occasion of the ruler’s 57th birthday. In a Facebook post today, Anwar prayed that Sultan Muhammad V and the entire royal family will always be blessed with His grace and guidance. Daulat Tuanku,” he said.

items.title: Health minister: Mission is to transform healthcare within 15th Parliament timeframe
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad wants the national healthcare transformation agenda, including modernising the system and improving patient service delivery, to be completed within the 15th parliamentary term. He said the Ministry of Health (MOH) faces a major challenge of not only keeping facilities ready but also ensuring healthcare delivery consistently meets the people’s needs. Dzulkefly said MOH faces increasingly complex challenges, including food safety and quality, mental health and planetary health.

items.title: Lawmakers welcome national suicide registry, urge strict service standards for crisis helplines
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Three DAP lawmakers have welcomed the launch of the National Suicide and Fatal Injury Registry Malaysia (NSFIRM) and the Ministry of Health’s Postvention Services Guidelines, while calling for stronger crisis helpline standards. In a joint statement, Bandar Kuching MP Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Wuen and state assemblymen Lim Yi Wei (Kampung Tunku) and Michelle Ng Mei Sze (Subang Jaya) said the launch, three years after attempted suicide was decriminalised, reaffirms the government’s commitment to mental health. They said that Malaysia previously lacked a systematic registry of suicide deaths and attempts.

items.title: Perak PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul Amir sworn in as senator
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Perak PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul Amir Sabri today took his oath of office as a Senator representing the state for a three-year term from Sept 10, 2026 to Sept 9, 2029. Mohamad Hairul Amir, 38, was sworn in before Dewan Negara President Datuk Awang Bemee Awang Ali Basah at a ceremony held at the Senate here. Meanwhile, Awang Bemee, in his speech, said Mohamad Hairul Amir’s broad experience spanning political leadership, public administration, government relations, community development and corporate governance would bring valuable insights to Senate debates and proceedings.

items.title: Loke: Transport Ministry to centralise bunkering licences from February 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — The Transport Ministry will assume sole authority for approving bunkering licences and related permits starting February 1, 2027. Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said that centralising these approvals will provide operators with a single point of accountability and ensure more consistent decisions regarding safety, fuel quality, and environmental protection. This will help to boost our bunkering sector, hopefully,” Loke said while officiating Malaysia Maritime Week 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre.

items.title: PM: Malaysians should have the choice to work past 60, ageing population needs options
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — With Malaysia expected to be an aged nation by 2048, the focus should not only be on ensuring sufficient retirement savings but also ensuring people have the choice to work past age 60, the prime minister said today. In Malaysia, the minimum retirement age for the private sector and the mandatory retirement age for civil servants are both currently at age 60. In his speech, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said those who want to work after age 60 should be given the choice, but did not say whether there are plans to raise the minimum or mandatory retirement age.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB meets Tuanku Muhriz amid royal dispute
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 29 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim was reportedly granted an audience with Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Istana Hinggap here today amid the state’s ongoing constitutional and customary dispute. The meeting was also understood to have been attended by Undang Luak Sungei Ujong Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari, Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid and Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad. Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had recently urged Ismail to meet Tuanku Muhriz and the Undang Yang Empat to seek a resolution to the dispute.

items.title: Loke says will stay as transport minister until Najib house arrest begins
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Anthony Loke Siew Fook today said that he will stay on as transport minister until former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak begins his house arrest. He said that he had submitted his resignation letter to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday, when they had discussed the matter further. So, the timeframe is that when Najib returns home, my resignation will take effect,” Loke told reporters after officiating Malaysia Maritime Week 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre.

items.title: High Court finds Putrajaya, Selangor authorities liable for Taman Sri Muda flood devastation
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 29 — The High Court has found the Malaysian government liable for damages caused by the catastrophic 2021 floods that devastated Taman Sri Muda in Shah Alam, citing a failure to promptly escalate disaster response and maintain effective mitigation systems. The court also found the director-general of the Selangor Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) and the Shah Alam City Council (MBSA) jointly liable with the federal government. The court rejected the defendants’ attempt to use an “act of God” defence, ruling it inapplicable when reasonable human intervention could have mitigated the disaster.

items.title: Avoid the F1 rush: AirAsia advises extra KLIA travel time Oct 2-4
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — AirAsia advises all guests travelling through the Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 2 to plan their journey, as higher passenger volumes and heavier traffic are expected in conjunction with the Formula 1 race weekend at Sepang International Circuit from Oct 2 to 4. The airlines said guests are advised to arrive at the airport at least three hours before the scheduled departure time for international flights and two hours before the scheduled departure time for domestic flights. “All guests, including those travelling under group bookings, are strongly encouraged to complete self check-in via the AirAsia MOVE app or our website.
